title: Despising God's Goodness
english: We can say to those who are being drawn away from God that they are despising the wealth of God's goodness, forbearance, and patience, being ignorant that God's goodness leads to repentance.
But due to your hardness and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and revelation and judgment of God.

For they are drawing near the time of punishment, perhaps being faint-hearted because they will be punished, and not committing sins unintentionally; instead, they are bringing judgment upon themselves without being forced to do so, and they are imposing the verdicts on themselves.
They are accumulating their sins and lawlessness, much like oxen bear a yoke and pull with great force, binding themselves to toil, and they are drawing their sins like a long rope.
Some have said, 'Let the Lord's plan come quickly so we can see it and know it' (Isaiah 5:19), which is a desire for the day of the Lord.
As another prophet has said, 'Woe to those who desire the day of the Lord,' for this day is darkness, not light, and a gloom without its radiance (Amos 5:18).
Therefore, we must learn that God is grieved and immediately repent and appease Him with unceasing prayers, rather than provoking Him further, and not despise Him when He threatens.
God is patient and merciful, forgiving lawlessness and passing over injustice, and to the small, sometimes with tears of the sinners, He changes to His most beloved calmness.
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness, who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter (Isaiah 5:20).
These individuals are wise in their own eyes and knowledgeable before themselves, but they are completely foolish.
Through their foolishness, God convicts those who have committed sins, like a long rope.
It is necessary for all to praise and repent, and through gentleness, to deliver themselves from the impending wrath.
They must appease the God who is grieved, the ruler of all, with fasts.
Unfortunately, the unworthy have become like money-changers, honoring the more shameful things and despising the incomparably better things, which are most profitable for their salvation.

Therefore, it is fitting for those who have thought in this way to say woe, for they have become unholy and foolish judges, saying that evil is good, counting darkness as light and bitter as sweet and sweet as bitter.

title: The Temple’s Glory and the Voice of the Seraphim
english: All the nations you have made shall come and bow down before you, Lord. This promise has been fulfilled in the gathering of the peoples called from among the nations.
And all who worship do so through the one who has become for us and remains through himself, above all things.

Then the temple’s lintel was lifted from the sound of their crying, and the house filled with smoke—just as the prophet saw the Lord of Hosts seated on a high and exalted throne, encircled by the holy Seraphim, who never cease to bless him with their praise.
Indeed, it was confirmed that the house was full of his glory.
Now he declares that the lintel was lifted, the house filled with smoke, and that this came from the voice with which the holy Seraphim cried out.
We must ask: Was that voice the cause of what happened to the house? Yet how could it be otherwise than foolish to suppose so? How then should we think about these matters? Best of all, and wisely.
Before our Savior took flesh and dwelt among us, while Israel still kept the law without hindrance or addition, that famous temple in Jerusalem, which Solomon built to the glory of God, was full.
They were completing...

title: Captivity and Conquest
english: The people will lie helpless, like walnuts that have fallen from their container, a situation that Solomon describes by comparing a bird that has fallen from its nest to a person who has been torn from their own place, saying, 'As a bird when it falls from its own nest, so a man when he is torn from his own places' (Proverbs 27:8), which highlights the pitiful state of those in captivity, who are trodden down and helpless under the power of their conquerors.

This plight is vividly illustrated in the historical narrative of the Scriptures, which tells us that during the reign of Ahaz, son of Joatham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, waged war against Jerusalem, but were unable to besiege it.

It seems that those who reject the historical narrative in the divinely inspired Scriptures flee from understanding the things written in them in the proper way, which is a shame, because spiritual theory, which is good and profitable, enlightens the eye of the mind, making it most intelligent.

When something from the historical events is brought to us through the sacred Scriptures, then we should seek the useful thing from history, so that the divinely inspired Scripture may appear to us as saving and beneficial from all sides, providing valuable insights and lessons.

The prophetic word sheds light on the events that occurred during the reign of Uzziah, affecting not only the tribes of Judah and Benjamin but also the ten tribes in Samaria, who were also called Ephraim and Israel.

Since the entire word of prophecy occurred during the times of four kings, the prophet sets forth the events happening in each time, indicating the order of the visions or his own words and assigning the best order.

After Azariah and Uzziah died, Jotham succeeded to the kingdom and followed the purpose and pursuits of his own father, doing what is right in the eyes of the Lord, just like Uzziah, except he did not remove the high places, but the people still burned incense on the high places.
Unlike Uzziah, who had sought to offer sacrifices to God and burn incense, and had been rebuked for this reason, Jotham did not attempt to do so.

After he died, Ahaz succeeded to the kingdom, during the reign of Pekah, son of Remaliah, over Israel, that is, the twelve tribes, and this man waged war against Ahaz and Judah, killing one hundred twenty thousand in one day.

The God of all was provoking Ahaz in his impieties, about which it is written in the fourth book of Kings that he walked in the way of the king of Israel (2 Kings 16:3), serving idols and passing his children through fire, sacrificing to the unclean demons.
